title: Up on the Roof: New York's Hidden Skyline Spaces

description.main: Alex MacLean's photographs of the rooftops of New York City, with maps, captions and an essay by Robert Campbell.
description.extended:
A book of photographs of New York City's rooftops by the aerial photographer Alex MacLean, showing the part of the city that usually stays hidden from the street.

Princeton Architectural Press published it in 2012. Beyond the familiar water towers, the photographs show rooftop pools, tennis courts, gardens, sunbathers, art and restaurants, and they make the case for the city's “green” potential. Maps and captions help the reader locate each image, and Robert Campbell contributes an essay that puts MacLean's work in context.

MacLean (born 1947) studied at Harvard College and the Harvard Graduate School of Design, earned a commercial pilot license in 1975 and founded Landslides Aerial Photography. He is best known for aerial photographs of the American landscape, from agricultural patterns to city grids, and is the author of ten books.
